title: Full mock 2
description: Second original full-length mock with new items. Sections 1–2 follow the TU Delft CST; section 3 adds the TU/e Algorithmic Thinking test.

questions.prompt: Solve for $x$: $4(x+1) = 2x + 10$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 4*(x+1)-(2*x+10); const r=h.roots(f,-50.3,50).map(x=> Math.round(x*1e9)/1e9); if(r.length!==1) throw new Error("expected one root, got "+r); return r[0];

questions.prompt: $f(x) = 2x^3 + x$. Compute $f'(1)$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 2*x**3+x; return h.deriv(f,1);

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\int_1^3 2x\,dx$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 2*x; return h.integrate(f,1,3);
return 16**0.75;

questions.prompt: What is $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$?

verifier.code: const v=Math.sin(Math.PI/4); const vals=[Math.SQRT2/2,0.5,Math.sqrt(3)/2,1]; const d=vals.map(x=> Math.abs(x-v)); const i=d.indexOf(Math.min(...d)); if(d[i]>1e-6*Math.max(1,Math.abs(v))) throw new Error("no option matches "+v); return {index:i};

questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 10 and a height of 7. What is its area?
$2x + y = 7$ and $x - y = 2$. Compute $x \cdot y$.

verifier.code: const s=[]; for(let x=-20;x<=20;x++) for(let y=-20;y<=20;y++) if(2*x+y===7 && x-y===2) s.push(x*y); if(s.length!==1) throw new Error("x"); return s[0];
const f=(x)=> 2*x-5-7; const r=h.roots(f,-50.3,50).map(x=> Math.round(x*1e9)/1e9); if(r.length!==1) throw new Error("expected one root, got "+r); return r[0];

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{4x+1}{2x-3}$.

verifier.code: const f=x=> (4*x+1)/(2*x-3); return f(1e9);

questions.prompt: $f(x) = x\ln x$. Compute $f'(e)$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> x*Math.log(x); return h.deriv(f,Math.E);

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of $f(x) = x + \dfrac{4}{x}$ for $x > 0$?

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> x+4/x; const a=(0.01), b=(50); let best=f(a); for(let i=1;i<=400000;i++) best=Math.min(best, f(a+(b-a)*i/400000)); return best;

questions.prompt: At which $x$ does $f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2$ have an inflection point?

verifier.code: const r=h.roots(x=> h.deriv2(t=> t**3+3*t*t, x), -10.3, 10, 20000); return Math.round(r[0]*1e4)/1e4;

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\int_1^2 (6x^2 - 2x)\,dx$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 6*x*x-2*x; return h.integrate(f,1,2);

questions.prompt: What is the mean value of $f(x) = 2x + 1$ on $[1, 5]$?

verifier.code: return h.integrate(x=> 2*x+1, 1, 5)/4;

questions.prompt: Solve $\log_2(x + 3) = 4$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> Math.log2(x+3)-4; const r=h.roots(f,-2.99,100).map(x=> Math.round(x*1e9)/1e9); if(r.length!==1) throw new Error("expected one root, got "+r); return r[0];

questions.prompt: What is the derivative of $f(x) = e^{\sin x}$?
questions.hint: Chain rule: outer derivative times inner derivative.

verifier.code: const f=x=> Math.exp(Math.sin(x)); const o=[x=> Math.cos(x)*Math.exp(Math.sin(x)), x=> Math.exp(Math.cos(x)), x=> Math.sin(x)*Math.exp(Math.sin(x)-1), x=> Math.exp(Math.sin(x))]; const xs=[0.3,1.2,2.5,4.1]; return {indices: o.flatMap((g,i)=> xs.every(x=> Math.abs(g(x)-h.deriv(f,x))<1e-6)?[i]:[])};

questions.prompt: The radius of a sphere grows at 1 cm/s. How fast is the volume growing when $r = 3$ cm?

verifier.code: const v=h.deriv(t=> 4/3*Math.PI*(3+t)**3, 0); const vals=[36*Math.PI,12*Math.PI,108*Math.PI,9*Math.PI]; const d=vals.map(x=> Math.abs(x-v)); const i=d.indexOf(Math.min(...d)); if(d[i]>1e-6*Math.max(1,Math.abs(v))) throw new Error("no option matches "+v); return {index:i};

questions.prompt: The region under $y = x$ for $0 \le x \le 3$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. What is the volume?

verifier.code: const v=Math.PI*h.integrate(x=> x*x, 0, 3); const vals=[9*Math.PI,27*Math.PI,3*Math.PI,4.5*Math.PI]; const d=vals.map(x=> Math.abs(x-v)); const i=d.indexOf(Math.min(...d)); if(d[i]>1e-6*Math.max(1,Math.abs(v))) throw new Error("no option matches "+v); return {index:i};

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all solutions of $\sin(2x) = 0$ in $[0, \pi)$?

verifier.code: const v=h.sum(h.roots(x=> Math.sin(2*x), -1e-7, Math.PI-1e-7)); const vals=[Math.PI/2,Math.PI,1.5*Math.PI,0]; const d=vals.map(x=> Math.abs(x-v)); const i=d.indexOf(Math.min(...d)); if(d[i]>1e-5*Math.max(1,Math.abs(v))) throw new Error("no option matches "+v); return {index:i};

questions.prompt: The tangent line to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 10$ at $(1, 3)$ crosses the $x$-axis at $(c, 0)$. What is $c$?
questions.hint: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius to (1, 3).
questions.explanation: The tangent at $(x_0, y_0)$ is $x_0x + y_0y = 10$: $x + 3y = 10$. With $y = 0$: $c = 10$.

verifier.code: const y=x=> Math.sqrt(10-x*x); const m=h.deriv(y,1); return 1 - y(1)/m;

questions.prompt: p and q are true and r is false. What is the value of (p ∧ q) → r?
questions.explanation: p ∧ q = T and r = F, so T → F = false.

questions.prompt: In how many of the 8 rows is p → (q ∧ r) true?
questions.hint: It is automatically true when p is false.
questions.explanation: p false: 4 rows, all true. p true: needs q ∧ r, 1 row. Total 5.

questions.prompt: Which formula is equivalent to ¬p → q?
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of ¬p → q is ¬q → ¬¬p, i.e. ¬q → p. (Also ≡ p ∨ q.)

questions.prompt: B(x): "x is a bird", F(x): "x can fly". Translate "Some birds cannot fly."
questions.explanation: There is an x that is a bird and cannot fly: ∃x (B(x) ∧ ¬F(x)).

verifier.code: const D=[0,1,2]; const un=[]; for(let m=0;m<8;m++) un.push(x=>((m>>x)&1)===1); const all=f=>D.every(f), ex=f=>D.some(f); const t=(B,F)=> D.some(x=> B(x) && !F(x)); const o=[(B,F)=> ex(x=> B(x)&&!F(x)), (B,F)=> ex(x=> !B(x)||!F(x)), (B,F)=> !all(x=> B(x)&&F(x)), (B,F)=> all(x=> !B(x)||!F(x))]; return {indices: o.flatMap((g,i)=> un.every(B=> un.every(F=> g(B,F)===t(B,F)))?[i]:[])};

questions.prompt: Is the argument "p ∨ q, ¬p, therefore q" valid?
p = "you pass", s = "you study". Translate "You pass only if you study."
s = "it is sunny", w = "it is a weekday", b = "we go to the beach". Translate: "Unless it is a weekday, we go to the beach if it is sunny."
questions.explanation: ¬w → (s → b), which is equivalent to (s ∧ ¬w) → b.

questions.prompt: In how many of the 8 rows is (p ↔ q) ∨ r true?
questions.hint: Count the rows where it is false instead.
questions.explanation: It is false only when p ↔ q is false (2 of the 4 pq-combinations) and r is false: 2 rows. So 8 − 2 = 6 rows are true.

questions.prompt: Simplify p ∧ (p ∨ q).
questions.explanation: If p is true, p ∨ q is true; if p is false, the conjunction is false. So p ∧ (p ∨ q) ≡ p.

questions.prompt: Which formula is equivalent to (p → q) ∨ (p → r)?
The domain is {1, 2, 3, 4}. Is ∀x ∃y (x + y = 5) true?
questions.hint: For each x, is 5 − x in the domain?
questions.explanation: x = 1, 2, 3, 4 need y = 4, 3, 2, 1 — all in the domain. True.

verifier.code: const D=[1,2,3,4]; return {index: D.every(x=> D.some(y=> x+y===5)) ? 0 : 1};

questions.prompt: Which statement is equivalent to ¬∀x (P(x) → Q(x))?
questions.hint: Push the negation in; ¬(A → B) ≡ A ∧ ¬B.

verifier.code: const D=[0,1,2]; const un=[]; for(let m=0;m<8;m++) un.push(x=>((m>>x)&1)===1); const all=f=>D.every(f), ex=f=>D.some(f); const t=(P,Q)=> !all(x=> !P(x)||Q(x)); const o=[(P,Q)=> ex(x=> P(x)&&!Q(x)), (P,Q)=> all(x=> !P(x)||!Q(x)), (P,Q)=> ex(x=> P(x)||Q(x)), (P,Q)=> all(x=> !P(x)&&Q(x))]; return {indices: o.flatMap((g,i)=> un.every(P=> un.every(Q=> g(P,Q)===t(P,Q)))?[i]:[])};

questions.prompt: Is this argument valid? "All A are B. Some C are not A. Therefore some C are not B."
questions.hint: The C's outside A might still be inside B.
questions.explanation: Counterexample: A = {1}, B = {1, 2}, C = {2}. Both premises hold but every C is a B. Invalid.

verifier.code: const N=4; const sets=[]; for(let m=0;m<(1<<N);m++) sets.push(Array.from({length:N},(_,i)=>((m>>i)&1)===1)); const S={all:(X,Y)=>X.every((x,i)=>!x||Y[i]), some:(X,Y)=>X.some((x,i)=>x&&Y[i]), no:(X,Y)=>X.every((x,i)=>!(x&&Y[i])), someNot:(X,Y)=>X.some((x,i)=>x&&!Y[i])}; const models=(k)=> h.tuples(sets,k);const ok=models(3).every(([A,B,C,D])=> !(S.all(A,B) && S.someNot(C,A)) || (S.someNot(C,B))); return {index: ok ? 0 : 1};

questions.prompt: From p → q, ¬q ∨ r and ¬r, what follows?
questions.explanation: ¬r with ¬q ∨ r gives ¬q; with p → q this gives ¬p.

questions.prompt: Knights always tell the truth; knaves always lie. A says "B is a knave." B says "A and C are both knights." C says "B is a knight." Who is a knight?
questions.explanation: If A were a knave, B would be a knight, but then B's claim makes A a knight — contradiction. So A is a knight, B is a knave, B's claim is false (so C is a knave), and C's claim "B is a knight" is indeed false.

verifier.code: const sols=h.tuples([true,false],3).filter(k=> [k=> !k[1],k=> k[0]&&k[2],k=> k[1]].every((s,i)=> s(k)===k[i])); const desc=(k)=> {const n=["A","B","C"].filter((_,i)=>k[i]); return n.length===0?"Nobody is a knight":n.length===3?"All three are knights":n.length===1?"Only "+n[0]+" is a knight":n.join(" and ")+" are knights";}; const got=[...new Set(sols.map(desc))]; if(got.length!==1) throw new Error("puzzle has "+sols.length+" solutions"); return got[0];

questions.prompt: In how many of the 16 rows (variables p, q, r, s) is (p → q) → (r → s) true?
questions.hint: Count the false rows: when is an implication between two implications false?
questions.explanation: It is false only when p → q is true (3 of 4 pq-rows) and r → s is false (r = T, s = F: 1 of 4). That is 3 false rows, so 16 − 3 = 13 true rows.

questions.prompt: Select **all** tautologies.
questions.hint: Name the rule behind each one, or find a falsifying row.
questions.explanation: 1 is modus ponens and 2 is modus tollens written as formulas — both tautologies. 3 (the converse) fails for p = F, q = T. 4 fails for p = T, q = F. 5: the conclusion q ∨ ¬q is always true — tautology.

questions.prompt: The domain is {1, 2, …, 10}. For how many x is ∀y (y divides x → (y = 1 ∨ y = x)) true?
questions.hint: Which numbers have no divisors other than 1 and themselves? Don't forget 1.
questions.explanation: The condition holds for the primes 2, 3, 5, 7 and also for x = 1 (its only divisor is 1). That makes 5.

verifier.code: const D=h.range(1,10); return D.filter(x=> D.every(y=> x%y!==0 || y===1 || y===x)).length;

questions.prompt: If Ann goes, Bob goes. If Bob goes, Cas does not go. Cas goes. What follows?
questions.explanation: Cas goes, so (by b → ¬c and modus tollens) Bob does not go; then (by a → b) Ann does not go.

questions.prompt: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U stand in a row. P is somewhere left of Q, Q is somewhere left of R, and S and T stand next to each other. How many orders are possible?
questions.hint: Glue S and T into a block, then handle P, Q, R.
questions.explanation: Treat S–T as a block (2 internal orders): 5 units give 5! = 120 orders, and P, Q, R appear in the required order in 1/6 of them: 20. Times 2 = 40.

verifier.code: return h.permutations(["P","Q","R","S","T","U"]).filter(o=>{const i=x=>o.indexOf(x); return i("P")<i("Q") && i("Q")<i("R") && Math.abs(i("S")-i("T"))===1;}).length;

questions.prompt: What number comes next? 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …

verifier.code: const s=[1,2,4,8,16]; if(!s.every((x,i)=> i===0||x===2*s[i-1])) throw new Error("x"); return 2*s[4];

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
x ← 10
x ← x − 3
x ← x · 2
print x

questions.prompt: Five people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes?

verifier.code: return h.combinations(h.range(1,5),2).length;

questions.prompt: Linear search in an unsorted list of 200 items: what is the maximum number of items inspected?
questions.hint: Worst case: the item is last or absent.

verifier.code: const A=h.range(1,200); let w=0; for(const t of [...A,-1]){ let k=0; for(const x of A){ k++; if(x===t) break; } w=Math.max(w,k); } return w;

questions.prompt: Write the decimal number 45 in binary.

verifier.code: return (45).toString(2);

questions.prompt: How many 3-letter strings can be made from the letters A, B, C, D if letters may repeat?

verifier.code: return h.tuples(["A","B","C","D"],3).length;

questions.prompt: Which letter comes next? A, B, D, G, K, …
questions.explanation: Positions 1, 2, 4, 7, 11: steps 1, 2, 3, 4. Next step 5 → position 16 = P.

verifier.code: const s=["A","B","D","G","K"].map(c=>c.charCodeAt(0)-64); const d=s.slice(1).map((x,i)=>x-s[i]); if(!d.every((x,i)=>i===0||x===d[i-1]+1)) throw new Error("x"); return String.fromCharCode(64+s[4]+d[3]+1);

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
s ← 0
for i from 1 to 10 step 3
  s ← s + i
print s

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
S ← []
for i from 1 to 5
  push(S, i)
  if i mod 2 = 0 then
    x ← pop(S)
print S[1] + S[length(S)]
questions.hint: Track the stack after every iteration.
questions.explanation: Push 1; push 2, pop; push 3; push 4, pop; push 5. The stack is [1, 3, 5]: S[1] + S[3] = 1 + 5 = 6.

questions.prompt: How many nodes are at distance exactly 2 (in number of edges) from A?
questions.code:
A — B
A — C
B — D
C — D
C — E
D — F
E — F
F — G
questions.explanation: Level 1: B, C. Level 2: D, E. Level 3: F. Level 4: G. Two nodes at distance 2.

verifier.code: const d=h.bfsDist(h.graph(["A-B","A-C","B-D","C-D","C-E","D-F","E-F","F-G"]),"A"); return Object.values(d).filter(x=> x===2).length;

questions.prompt: How many nodes of this graph have odd degree?
questions.code:
A — B
A — C
A — D
B — C
C — D
D — E
questions.hint: Count the edges at each node.
questions.explanation: Degrees: A 3, B 2, C 3, D 3, E 1. Odd: A, C, D, E — 4 nodes (so no Euler path exists).

verifier.code: const g=h.graph(["A-B","A-C","A-D","B-C","C-D","D-E"]); return Object.values(g).filter(n=> n.length%2===1).length;

questions.prompt: How many single shifts does insertion sort perform to sort [3, 1, 2, 5, 4]?
questions.hint: Each shift fixes one inverted pair.

verifier.code: const A=[3,1,2,5,4]; let s=0; for(let i=1;i<A.length;i++){ const k=A[i]; let j=i-1; while(j>=0 && A[j]>k){ A[j+1]=A[j]; j--; s++; } A[j+1]=k; } return s;

questions.prompt: How many of the numbers 1, 2, …, 60 are divisible by 3 or by 4?
questions.hint: Count each and subtract the overlap (multiples of 12).

verifier.code: return h.range(1,60).filter(n=> n%3===0 || n%4===0).length;

questions.prompt: Compute 22 AND 13.

verifier.code: return 22 & 13;

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.hint: Each call keeps the value mod 9 the same while making it smaller.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.code:
A ← [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
for i from 1 to 4
  A[i + 1] ← A[i + 1] + A[i]
for i from 5 down to 2
  A[i] ← A[i] − A[i − 1]
print A
questions.hint: The first loop builds running totals; what does the second loop undo?
questions.explanation: Loop 1 turns A into [1, 3, 6, 10, 15]. Loop 2 runs from the back and replaces each element by its difference with the previous one, restoring [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. (Running it forwards instead would give a different result.)

questions.prompt: Adjacent nodes must get different colours. What is the minimum number of colours needed for this graph?
questions.code:
A — B
B — C
C — A
D — A
D — B
E — C
E — D
questions.explanation: A, B, C form a triangle, so at least 3 colours. Three suffice: A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, D = 3, E = 1.

verifier.code: const N=["A","B","C","D","E"]; const E=[["A","B"],["B","C"],["C","A"],["D","A"],["D","B"],["E","C"],["E","D"]]; for(let k=1;k<=5;k++){ if(h.tuples(h.range(1,k),5).some(c=> E.every(([a,b])=> c[N.indexOf(a)]!==c[N.indexOf(b)]))) return k; }

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
i ← 1
k ← 0
while i < 1000
  i ← i · 3 + 1
  k ← k + 1
print k

questions.prompt: In how many ways can a 2 × 8 board be covered with 1 × 2 dominoes?
questions.hint: Look at the left edge: one vertical domino, or two horizontal ones stacked.

verifier.code: const W=n=> n<=1 ? 1 : W(n-1)+W(n-2); let brute=0; const go=(col)=>{ if(col===8){ brute++; return; } if(col>8) return; go(col+1); go(col+2); }; go(0); if(brute!==W(8)) throw new Error("x"); return brute;

questions.prompt: A machine reads a 5-bit string from left to right with state r ∈ {0, 1, 2}, starting at 0; bit b changes r to (2r + b) mod 3. It accepts if it ends in 0. How many of the 32 strings of length 5 does it accept?
questions.explanation: r is the value of the bits read so far, mod 3. Accepted strings are the binary representations (with leading zeros) of the multiples of 3 from 0 to 31: 0, 3, …, 30 — 11 numbers.

verifier.code: return h.tuples([0,1],5).filter(t=> t.reduce((r,b)=> (2*r+b)%3, 0)===0).length;
